newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gov't railway stake to 33.5 pct - officials.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gov't railway stake to 33.5 pct - officials.

text.p: Officials from Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and the Mexican government said Monday the government committed to a maximum 33.5 percent stake in the Northeast Railway after the company approached the government with credit problems.

TMM and Kansas City Southern Industries, through joint venture Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM) won 50-year operating rights to the key trade route, after bidding almost three times higher than competitors.

"We saw that credit was more expensive because TFM bid the highest. There was a huge difference between the second highest bidders, so banks had second thoughts," privatization director Jorge Silberstein with the Communications and Transport Ministry told Reuters.
Silberstein said the government committed up to a $237.5 million equity stake after approached by TFM.
Merrill Lynch and Chase Manhattan had originally planned to provide financing aid, but Morgan Stanley was TFM's final financial assessor.
The government will not purchase its stake until the second payment for the railway of about $840 million, which is due by July 31, TMM spokesman Fernando Ruiz aid.
Silberstein said the government's involvement will be "temporary," with a resale to TFM, "as soon as possible."

Added to the 20-percent share of the railway retained by the government, a maximum $237.5 million equity position in TFM could leave the government with a total stake in the railway of about 33.5 percent.
"We want to give credit for the investment plan proposed because it is extremely good and we don't want the interest expense to be a burden on operations," he said.

As analysts and traders processed last Thursday's announcement that the government would take a stake in the railway, TMM's shares recovered slightly to 39.8 pesos in late trading, from a low 34 pesos a week ago.

"If the railroad concession proves to be successful they have the option to buy out the government by the end of year four.... If on the other hand, the projections fail to materialize, they would have an additional partner to share the burden and a relative inexpensive source of financing," Bear, Stearns analyst Santiago Pique wrote in a report.

TFM will finance its remaining payments with a $750 million package, composed of $325 million from U.S. banks term loans priced at Libor plus between 3.5 to 4.0 percent with a maturity of about five years, and $400 million from a bridge one-year loan convertible to a six-year rollover note, he said.
In addition, Pique wrote, the company plans to emit $250 zero-coupon bonds and a $150 ten-year Yankee bond.
